chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a fence between two houses, so he claimed that Ali (peace be upon him) judged with it for the owner of the house whose side the fence was facing.

key_terms.الْقِمَاطِ: The facing side or front of the house
key_terms.خُصٍّ: A fence or partition wall separating properties

ai.seo_question: How is ownership of a boundary fence determined between two houses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *al-qada'* (judicial ruling) by Imam Ali (AS) in resolving property disputes, highlighting the importance of structural orientation (*qimat*) in determining boundary rights. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise legal reasoning (*ijtihad*) derived from the Imams' judgments to ensure justice in communal living. The ruling reflects the broader Islamic principle of preserving neighbors' rights (*haqq al-jar*) and preventing encroachment.
